Notes: Math Mate — Asset List for Design Team. Currently the app uses emojis and CSS animations as placeholders. This list covers what's needed for the full visual reskin.
Two characters: a Master Tutor (primary teaching voice) and a Sidekick/Minion (cute companion for nudges and light humor)

Description / Purpose: The tutor's resting state. Visible in the chat panel area and content pane when speaking. Friendly, approachable, teacher-like.
Notes: This is the primary character asset — everything else builds on this design

Description / Purpose: Tutor is talking (mouth open/moving). Shown whenever AI voice is playing (narration, questions, scaffolding).
Notes: Most frequently seen state — needs to feel natural and not repetitive

Description / Purpose: Tutor is paying attention to the student. Shown when student holds PTT and speaks.
Variants / States: Looping animation (e.g. ear cupped or leaning in)
Notes: Should feel attentive — kid should feel heard

Description / Purpose: Tutor is processing what the student said. Brief state between student speaking and AI responding.
Variants / States: Looping animation (e.g. hand on chin or looking up)
Notes: Shown for 1-3 seconds. Can be simpler than speaking/listening.

Description / Purpose: Tutor is happy/excited. Shown when student answers correctly, alongside confetti.
Variants / States: One-shot animation (e.g. arms up or clapping)
Notes: Triggered on correct answers — needs to feel genuinely excited

Description / Purpose: Tutor is warm and supportive. Shown when student answers incorrectly. Must NOT look disappointed.
Notes: Critical: never sad or frustrated. Think 'good try, let's figure it out together'

Description / Purpose: Tutor waves hello. Shown on welcome screen and during greeting conversation.
Notes: First impression — sets the tone for the whole session

Description / Purpose: The sidekick's resting pose. Small, cute, sits near the chat area or corner of screen. Not attention-stealing.
Notes: Should be noticeably smaller than the tutor — a companion not a co-teacher

Description / Purpose: Sidekick pokes or waves to get student's attention. Used when student is supposed to talk but hasn't pressed PTT.
Notes: Playful 'hey, your turn!' energy. Replaces the current text-only prompt

Description / Purpose: Sidekick does a little happy dance or jump. Shown alongside tutor celebration on correct answers.
Notes: Secondary celebration — smaller and quicker than tutor's

Description / Purpose: Ambient idle animation. Sidekick does something cute occasionally (yawns, scratches head, looks around). Keeps the screen feeling alive.
Notes: These are the personality moments — small things that make kids smile
Replacing the current CSS-only Candy Land background

Description / Purpose: Main app background visible behind all content. Should be warm, inviting, not distracting. Think classroom or adventure world.
Variants / States: 1 main version (can be tiled or stretched). Optional: subtle parallax layers
Notes: Must not compete with content for attention. Soft colors.

Description / Purpose: Landing page background when the app first loads. Can be more vibrant/exciting than the in-session background.
Notes: This is the 'cover page' — can be more expressive

Description / Purpose: Celebration background shown when student finishes all 14 nodes. Festive, achievement-focused.
Notes: Should feel like a culmination — balloons/stars/party vibe

Description / Purpose: Background or frame for the chat sidebar where conversation bubbles appear. Currently a plain translucent panel.
Notes: Needs to be tall and narrow — sidebar on desktop; bottom overlay on mobile

Description / Purpose: Message bubble shape for tutor messages. Currently white rounded rectangle.
Variants / States: 1 shape (can include small tutor avatar thumbnail)
Notes: WhatsApp-style. Tutor bubble should be visually distinct from student bubble

Description / Purpose: Message bubble shape for student messages. Currently green rounded rectangle.
Notes: Could stay simpler than tutor bubble — student messages are short

Description / Purpose: Optional decorative frame around the main content area (where slides, videos, applets appear).
Notes: Light touch — don't obscure content edges. Could be just rounded corners with a subtle border

Description / Purpose: Hold-to-talk button in the chat panel. Currently emoji mic + CSS. The primary student interaction control.
Notes: Most tapped element in the app. Must be large, clear, and finger-friendly

Description / Purpose: Visual feedback while student is holding the button and speaking. Currently CSS waveform bars.
Notes: Should feel responsive — 'yes I can hear you'

Description / Purpose: Skip/Done button shown on videos, applets, and slides (top-right corner). Currently a translucent pill with arrow text.
Notes: Small, unobtrusive but findable

Description / Purpose: 'Let's Go' button on the welcome screen.
Notes: Big and inviting — the call to action
Note: the current top progress bar with 14 star milestones is being removed. Replaced with something simpler.

Description / Purpose: Small icon awarded per completed node. Could be a star, gem, or custom collectible.
Notes: 14 total across the journey. Only needed if we keep any progress visualization

Description / Purpose: Shown on completion screen. Currently a trophy emoji.
Notes: Could be a badge or certificate or medal — whatever fits the character theme

Description / Purpose: Triggered on correct answers. Currently CSS confetti pieces. Could become themed particles (stars, sparkles, fraction symbols).
Notes: Should match the overall visual style — not generic confetti

Description / Purpose: Transition between nodes (e.g. from video to post-question). Currently an instant cut.
Notes: Keep it fast (300-500ms). Just enough to feel polished not sluggish

Description / Purpose: Brief visual reward overlaid on content when student answers correctly, just before confetti.
Variants / States: One-shot (e.g. green glow or checkmark burst)
Notes: Optional — confetti may be sufficient on its own
Not visual but worth listing since the design team may coordinate with audio

Description / Purpose: Short positive chime on correct answer.
Notes: Currently no SFX — purely voice-driven. Adding this would enhance the celebration moment

Description / Purpose: Subtle 'whoosh' or 'ding' when moving to the next node.
Notes: Optional polish

Description / Purpose: Brief click or beep when student starts/stops recording.
Notes: Gives tactile feedback that the mic is active
